proposal.blind_spot: Only load-side coalescing and no launch geometry are measured, so the optimizer cannot tell whether the saturated DRAM traffic is inflated by scattered stores or whether sub-peak DRAM utilization is caused by an undersized grid.

rationale.smsp__sass_average_data_bytes_per_sector: HIGH -> stores already coalesced, stop coalescing fixes and instead cut total bytes via fusion/avoiding intermediate materialization or accept ~1x / LOW -> writes are scattered, remap program ids so output offsets are contiguous (gather inputs instead of scattering outputs) or stage stores through shared memory to recoalesce them
rationale.launch__waves_per_multiprocessor: HIGH -> grid already saturates the GPU, keep per-program work and register/smem usage flat and treat DRAM bandwidth as the hard wall / LOW -> grid underfills the GPU or has a tail, shrink BLOCK and launch more programs or flatten to a larger grid to push DRAM utilization to peak

split.chosen_by: llm_tiebreak:It uses DRAM percent-of-peak—an actual saturation signal—at the stricter near-peak cut together with high DRAM write volume, so it marks store-heavy bandwidth-bound kernels more directly than the stall-based rule.
